title: Graceful queue drain, priority shed and idempotent replay safeguard for hosted API under tenant surges
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Several enterprise customers escalated after observing correlated 5xx spikes and long-tail timeouts during large batch uploads and tenant migrations. Root analysis shows a mismatch between edge admission (per-tenant rate limiter) and backend pool admission leading to request queuing, connection hold, and amplified client retries. This ticket implements a three-part mitigation: (1) a graceful queue drain/early-abort policy at the edge when backend admission is saturated, (2) a priority shedding controller to favor SLA tiers and customer bridge sessions during surge, and (3) an idempotent-replay token flow to allow safe client retries without duplicate model executions. The goal is to reduce 5xx waves, shorten tail latency, and provide clear customer-facing behavior during escalations.
acceptance_criteria: Edge queue depth for any tenant must not exceed configured safe threshold for more than 60s in normal traffic patterns
When backend pool admission drops below threshold, edge must return deterministic 429/503 with Retry-After for low-priority tenants and preserve streaming sessions for priority customers
Idempotent replay tokens issued for resumable requests must prevent duplicate model execution (verified by request fingerprint and dedup table)
Automated smoke test against staging reproduces tenant surge and demonstrates <25% reduction in observable 5xx rate and >40% reduction in median tail latency in affected paths
Runbook updated and on-call notified; customer communications draft available for two escalated accounts
technical_notes: Design: implement admission controller token bucket at edge + short-lived admission lease from backend. Edge keeps per-tenant in-flight counters and global admission window.

Queue drain policy: when backend signals saturation, edge starts draining non-priority queues with graceful 5s soft window and patches any in-flight streaming to attempt fast close if resumable flag present.
Priority shed controller: configurable tiers (P0, P1, P2) with mapping from customer attributes. During surge, P1/P2 get 429 with Retry-After; P0 retained with preemption of P2 in-flight where safe.

Idempotency: issue short-lived replay tokens (opaque UUID), store dedup entry in Redis with TTL aligned to model execution window. Token validation performed at runtime to skip re-execution if duplicate seen.
Metrics and tracing: new metric tenant.queue_drain_events, tenant.preempt_count, idempotency.dedup_hits and spans for admission decision path. Tag events with escalation_id for correlation.
Compatibility: must interoperate with Dedicated and Private routing; fallback policy to compatible model variant (quantized) remains unchanged.

Trade-offs: early abort increases 429 surface area which may annoy customers; mitigated via customer-bridge whitelist and clear comms. Dedup table introduces small storage/lookup cost but avoids expensive duplicate GPU work.

risks: Risk: Incorrect priority mappings could cut off a paying customer — mitigation: customer-bridge whitelist and manual override via console
Risk: Dedup TTL mismatch could either replay after eviction or leak entries — mitigation: conservative TTL and background compaction job
Risk: Additional Redis lookups may add latency to hot paths — mitigation: batch lookup for multi-request sessions and local LRU caching
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): edge admission and queue-drain enabled for 10% of non-critical tenants; idempotency enabled only for resumable uploads
Phase 2 (ramp): increase to 50% after 48h if dashboard shows stable error rate and no false positives
Phase 3 (opt-in for critical): enable priority shed controls for specific customers with Solutions Engineer coordination
Fallthrough: global disable toggle in console and kill switch in oncall runbook
